items.title: U.S. Stocks Notch Fresh Record After Jobs Report Eases Rate-Hike Fears
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed at a record Friday after a weak jobs report eased investors’ fears of an interest-rate hike in September.  The U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, an unexpected decline compared with the 83,000 job gains estimated by economists.  The unemployment rate ticked lower to 4.1% as more Americans stepped back from the labor market entirely.

items.title: Traders Scale Back Bets on Rate Hike
items.summary: Friday’s weaker-than-expected jobs report has flipped the market-based odds of whether the Federal Reserve raises interest rate in September. Interest-rate futures now show a 56% chance that the Fed stays on hold at its next meeting and a 44% chance of a rate hike, according to CME Group data.
